title: Who's Doing the Work? Who Owns the Result? | RACI Explained
section: The distinctions that prevent document failure
afterParagraph: Responsible is the role doing or coordinating the work. Accountable is the role answerable for the result and approval. Consulted roles provide input before action; informed roles receive relevant information after or during the event. A RACI row should describe an outcome or meaningful activity. If rows are every mouse click, the matrix becomes unreadable; if a row says only ‘operations’, it is too broad to expose ownership. Accountability does not automatically grant unlimited authority. A duty manager may own service recovery while needing commercial approval above a defined additional-cost threshold. Communication responsibility is separate from decision authority. One manager may approve the alternative coach while an assigned guest-facing role communicates the verified plan using the approved message.
rationale: An excursion pickup change illustrates responsible, accountable, consulted and informed roles.

title: Lean Explained in 60 Seconds | Hotel Check-In Example #leansixsigma #processimprovement
afterParagraph: Frameworks operate at different levels. ITIL contributes service and value-system thinking; PMP contributes temporary change delivery; Lean contributes flow, waste, and learning; Six Sigma contributes operational definitions, measurement, analysis, and control. The SOP remains the organization's tailored control. Integration should remove gaps, not create a giant template. Each stage produces only the evidence needed for the next decision and the eventual controlled process pack. Simple, low-risk work should use a proportionate version of the lifecycle. The lifecycle is iterative. Measurement, audit, incidents, user feedback, supplier performance, and changed conditions can return the team to value, mapping, risk, causes, or design. A published SOP is a controlled hypothesis about reliable work, not the final truth. Governance connects the stages through ownership, decisions, versions, evidence, and traceability. Without one accountable process owner and defined approval authority, integration becomes a collection of workshops with no controlled outcome.
rationale: A hotel check-in example explains the Lean contribution to this integrated model: understand guest value and improve flow before removing work.
